tags.description: Holds light: mends flesh, reveals what hides, steadies the heart.
Heavy and slow: binds, endures, draws every effect out.
Restless humours: speed, storms, and a temper to match.
Eats what it touches: dissolves, purges, cuts through.
Drawn from the grave: shadow, silence, the borrowed strength of death.
Cold that keeps: wards, preserves, numbs.
Speaks to the mind: visions, senses, other people's thoughts.
Fire in a bottle: breath, warmth and courage.
Living sap and root: healing, growth, the goodwill of beasts.
Raw spellwork, barely bottled: blinking, vanishing, remembering magic.

Applying it takes 1 minute: one creature, one weapon, or up to three pieces of ammunition can be coated with a single vial.

As a Utilize action, you can shatter the vial at a point within 20 feet. It bursts into a 5-foot-radius cloud, and the first creature to breathe it (normally one inside the cloud, DM's choice) gains the effect.

oddities: The liquid always settles level, however the bottle is tilted.
It hums a single low note when shaken.
It leaves the drinker's tongue violet for an hour.
For a minute after drinking, your reflection lags a heartbeat behind you.
A faint smell of rain follows the drinker for the rest of the day.
The vial is warm to the touch, even buried in snow.
The stopper bears a tiny thumbprint that matches no one in the party.
The bubbles inside rise in time with the holder's heartbeat.
Cats find the empty bottle irresistible.
The bottle casts a shadow a shade too dark.
Swirled, it shows for an instant a word in a language no one can name.
It tastes different to every person who sips it.
The drinker's voice drops an octave for ten minutes.
The empty vial rings like a small bell when tapped.
For an hour after drinking, nearby candle flames lean towards you.
A single hair on the drinker's head turns silver, for good.
It refuses to pour faster than a slow trickle.
Moths gather on the bottle at night.
The drinker dreams that night of the same unfamiliar door.
The liquid inside never quite stops moving.
The drinker hiccups a few harmless motes of light for a minute.
Held to the ear, the vial sounds like distant surf.
It smells faintly of whatever the drinker last ate.
Whoever drinks it remembers, briefly and clearly, their earliest memory.
